newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen poised to reap restructuring gains.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen poised to reap restructuring gains.

text.p: German steel company Thyssen AG on Tuesday predicted a hike in its full-year profits after divestment proceeds boosted first-half 1996/97 pretax earnings by 81 percent to 631 million marks ($372.6 million).

The divestments also caused sales in the six months ending March 31 to fall 2.7 percent to 17.9 billion marks ($10.6 billion) and lowered orders 1.6 percent to 17.8 billion marks ($10.5 billion), Thyssen said.

But the company said its improved business structure would lead to "a distinct business upswing" in the second half of the year ending Sept. 30. "The restructuring measures are beginning to bear fruit," the company said in a statement.
Adjusted for the effects of the divestments, sales rose 2 percent and pretax profit 22 percent, Thyssen said.
At 6 a.m. EDT, Thyssen shares were up 6 marks ($3.54) at 398.50 marks ($238.38), with the blue-chip DAX index up 0.3 percent at 3,668.92.
Even without the effect of its divestments, Thyssen had a solid first half and was on track to see profit rise next year, said Merrill Lynch analyst Alan Coats.

"This is a good result, but it was an intermediate year," he told Reuters. "The big gain should be in 1998. We should see greatly improved steel results based on steel prices going up very sharply, and improvement in capital goods margins."
Weak steel prices eroded profit from Thyssen's stainless steel operation in the first half of 1996/97, Coats said.

Thyssen has sold off defence, pumps, coal and metals businesses to focus on its elevator, auto parts, flat steel, production systems and raw materials units. It has also agreed to merge its steel operations with rival Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp.
